author.name: Siamul Karim Khan
author.affiliation: Software Engineer at Google | Ph.D. University of Notre Dame

publications.title: Lowering the Barrier to IREX Participation: Open-Source Algorithms, Toolkit, and Benchmarking for Iris Recognition
publications.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.20735 / Under revision at IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science (T-BIOM)
publications.abstract: IREX (Iris Exchange) evaluation programs present steep engineering barriers because academic algorithms must be compliant with strict C++ APIs and runtime constraints. We provide the first comprehensive, IREX X-compliant open-source ecosystem, open-source ArcIris and TripletIris baseline matchers, newly trained segmentation models, and standardized benchmarks across eight diverse datasets.

publications.title: Is There Evidence of Gender Bias in Iris Presentation Attack Detection Approaches?
publications.venue: IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science (T-BIOM)
publications.abstract: Biometric fairness and demographic neutrality are imperative for deployed security systems. This study investigates whether modern deep learning and hand-crafted iris presentation attack detection (PAD) algorithms exhibit disparate error rates across male and female demographic groups.

publications.title: EyePreserve: Identity-preserving iris synthesis
publications.venue: IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science (T-BIOM)
publications.abstract: Synthetic biometric generation faces the critical challenge of identity preservation across multiple intra-class acquisitions. We present EyePreserve, an identity-preserving iris synthesis framework leveraging generative adversarial networks and diffusion models to produce high-fidelity synthetic eye images with controllable pupil dynamics, illumination variations, and consistent iris identity templates.

publications.title: Gradient-Guided Exploration of Generative Model's Latent Space for Controlled Iris Image Augmentations
publications.abstract: Training robust iris recognition models requires extensive data diversity. We propose a gradient-guided latent space exploration method that systematically perturbs generative latent vectors to synthesize controlled variations in pupil size, occlusion, and lighting while strictly preserving subject biometric identity.

publications.title: Iris Liveness Detection Competition (LivDet-Iris) – The 2025 Edition
publications.venue: 2025 IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB)
publications.abstract: LivDet-Iris 2025 evaluates state-of-the-art iris presentation attack detection (PAD) algorithms against sophisticated physical and digital attack vectors, including textured contact lenses, prosthetic eyes, printed artifacts, and generative deepfake syntheses across multiple sequestered test datasets.

publications.title: University of Notre Dame Open Source Iris Recognition Repository
publications.venue: Notre Dame Computer Vision Research Laboratory (CVRL)
publications.abstract: An official open-source repository establishing standardized baseline algorithms, feature extractors, segmentation networks, and reproducibility benchmarks for contemporary iris biometrics research.

publications.title: Liveness detection
publications.venue: U.S. Patent Application 18/625,685 (Publication No. US 2024/0334008 A1)
publications.abstract: Methods, apparatus, and non-transitory computer readable media for biometric liveness detection and presentation attack mitigation via spatial-temporal feature decomposition and optical reflectance analysis.

publications.title: Deception detection
publications.venue: U.S. Patent Application 18/115,414 (Publication No. US 2023/0274582 A1)
publications.abstract: Systems, methods, and computer-readable media for automated, remote non-contact deception detection utilizing multimodal computer vision frameworks, facial micro-movement analysis, and remote physiological signal extraction from video streams.

publications.title: DeformIrisNet: An Identity-Preserving Model of Iris Texture Deformation
publications.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
publications.abstract: Pupil dilation and constriction induce non-linear, non-elastic deformations in human iris textures, degrading biometric recognition accuracy. We propose DeformIrisNet, a deep learning architecture that directly models pupil-dynamics-induced iris texture deformations while strictly preserving biometric identity. DeformIrisNet outperforms classical rubber-sheet linear normalization models across multiple benchmark datasets.

publications.title: Deception Detection and Remote Physiological Monitoring: A Dataset and Baseline Experimental Results
publications.venue: IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science (T-BIOM)
publications.abstract: Automated deception detection from video streams is a challenging problem with significant security and legal applications. We present a novel, publicly available multimodal dataset for deception detection comprising synchronized high-resolution video and physiological monitoring signals. We establish baseline experimental results demonstrating the utility of remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) and facial action units for deception prediction.

publications.title: PhotoStylist: Altering the Style of Photos Based on the Connotations of Texts
publications.venue: Advances in Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (PAKDD 2021), LNCS vol 12712, Springer
publications.abstract: Conveying abstract emotional connotations through visual photography is challenging. We introduce PhotoStylist, a cross-modal deep learning framework that alters the photographic style (color tones, lighting, contrast) of target images based on the connotation of accompanying textual captions.

publications.title: CaMR: Towards Connotation-aware Music Retrieval on Social Media with Visual Inputs
publications.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Advances in Social Networks Analysis and Mining (ASONAM)
publications.abstract: Background music selection for user-generated multimedia posts on social media requires understanding subtle emotional connotations beyond literal visual objects. We present CaMR, a connotation-aware music retrieval model that maps visual semantics and latent affective signals to relevant musical acoustic features, significantly outperforming traditional content-based retrieval baselines.

publications.title: A CNN-based approach to classify cricket bowlers based on their bowling actions
publications.venue: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication & Systems (SPICSCON)
publications.abstract: Cricket bowling action classification is a critical component for automated sports analytics, broadcast enhancement, and biomechanical legality assessment. This paper presents a convolutional neural network (CNN) framework using transfer learning on pre-trained deep architectures (including VGG16) to accurately classify bowlers based on sequential video frames and kinematic delivery actions.
